Research_Question: RQ1: Which attributes are associated with hotel booking cancellations?
Primary_Finding: Cancellations are overwhelmingly driven by 7 core behavioral, operational, and market features.
Statistical_Evidence: Deposit Type (Chi2=27,639.52, p<1e-300, Cramér V=0.4815); Lead Time (t=98.94, p<1e-300, Cohen d=0.6342, Mann-Whitney U=2.28e9); Market Segment (Chi2=8,499.93, p<1e-300, Cramér V=0.2670); Country PRT (Chi2=12,195.42); Special Requests (Rank 5, Gain=0.0520); Room Type Changed (Rank 6, Gain=0.0452); Car Parking Spaces (Rank 9, 0% cancel rate when >0).
Theoretical_Mechanism: Non-refundable deposits act as a proxy for speculative wholesale tour-group bookings with 99.4% cancellation rates. Longer lead times introduce heightened life-event uncertainty. Special requests and parking reflect strong guest commitment/skin-in-the-game.
Curricular_Verdict: Confirmed: Statistically significant associations verified via parametric, non-parametric, and tree-importance consensus.

Research_Question: RQ2: Which machine learning algorithm performs best?
Primary_Finding: LightGBM is the decisive global champion across all performance, calibration, and efficiency dimensions.
Statistical_Evidence: LightGBM: Test ROC-AUC = 0.9621 (1st), PR-AUC = 0.9433 (1st), Accuracy = 89.19% (1st), Positive F1 = 0.8519 (1st), Brier Score = 0.0750 (1st - lowest error), Training Time = 2.73s (10x faster than RF, 20x faster than MLP), Optimized Operational Loss = $381,516 (1st - lowest cost).
Theoretical_Mechanism: Histogram-based binning and leaf-wise (best-first) tree expansion capture complex asymmetric feature interactions far more effectively than depth-wise trees or distance-based heuristics.
Curricular_Verdict: Confirmed: LightGBM dominates XGBoost, Random Forest, MLP, Decision Tree, and KNN across all metrics.

Research_Question: RQ3: How much do hyperparameter adjustments improve model performance?
Primary_Finding: Hyperparameter tuning produces dramatic gains for unconstrained learners, but modest gains for robust ensembles.
Statistical_Evidence: Decision Tree ROC-AUC increased by +7.63% (0.8610 -> 0.9373); KNN ROC-AUC improved by +3.38% (0.9025 -> 0.9363); LightGBM improved by +1.04% (0.9517 -> 0.9621); XGBoost improved by +0.45% (0.9543 -> 0.9588); MLP improved by +0.27% (0.9439 -> 0.9466); Random Forest changed by -0.29% (0.9589 -> 0.9560).
Theoretical_Mechanism: Constraining unpruned Decision Trees and adopting Manhattan distance in KNN directly mitigated variance and the curse of dimensionality. Breimans Random Forest defaults are already mathematically near-optimal on tabular data.
Curricular_Verdict: Confirmed: Gains are highly architecture-dependent; weak learners benefit substantially, while bagging defaults require minimal tuning.

Research_Question: RQ4: Does feature selection improve model performance?
Primary_Finding: Selecting top features preserves >99.9% of discrimination while slashing memory by 80% and latency by ~45%.
Statistical_Evidence: At k=50 features (19.5% of total 257 features), LightGBM retains 99.91% of ROC-AUC (0.9612 vs 0.9621) with 89.17% accuracy. At k=100-150 features, test accuracy marginally increases to 89.32% and F1 rises to 0.8531, while inference latency drops from 25.2us to 13.5us per sample.
Theoretical_Mechanism: Pruning over 100 near-zero variance one-hot categorical dummies (rare country codes) acts as a structural regularizer, removing noisy leaf splits without discarding genuine predictive signal.
Curricular_Verdict: Confirmed: Supervised feature selection yields substantial computational efficiency and marginal variance reduction.

Research_Question: RQ5: Does dimensionality reduction using PCA improve or reduce performance?
Primary_Finding: PCA consistently and significantly degrades classifier performance across all tree-based tabular architectures.
Statistical_Evidence: LightGBM ROC-AUC plummeted from 0.9621 (full features) to 0.9134 at PCA-10 (-0.0487), 0.9411 at PCA-25 (-0.0210), and 0.9478 at PCA-50 (-0.0143). Random Forest dropped from 0.9560 to 0.9140 at PCA-10. Even at 100 components (99.9% variance), tree performance remained degraded.
Theoretical_Mechanism: Diagonal Boundary Destruction: Tree algorithms split orthogonally along single axes. Unsupervised linear combinations of sparse binary dummies force trees to approximate diagonal decision boundaries using complex step-functions.
Curricular_Verdict: Confirmed: PCA is counterproductive for tree-based tabular learning; supervised feature selection is strictly superior.

Research_Question: RQ6: How well do the models generalize to unseen data?
Primary_Finding: All tuned architectures demonstrate exceptional out-of-sample generalization with virtually zero generalization gap.
Statistical_Evidence: Tuned LightGBM 5-fold CV ROC-AUC = 0.9580 +/- 0.0010 vs. Held-Out Test ROC-AUC = 0.9621 (Delta = +0.0041). XGBoost CV = 0.9558 vs. Test = 0.9588 (+0.0030). Random Forest CV = 0.9517 vs. Test = 0.9560 (+0.0043). Zero negative generalization gap across all models.
Theoretical_Mechanism: Strict leakage-prevention pipeline: Preprocessing transformers and scaling statistics were fitted strictly on the 95,366 training instances and applied downstream to the 23,842 held-out test instances.
Curricular_Verdict: Confirmed: Models exhibit robust external validity and zero data leakage.
